body.statement: Suppose \((G,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\) and a three-view decomposition has recovered \(\mathscr L(P_X)\) and the component conditional columns up to one arbitrary permutation. The observable family \(\mathcal E(P_X)\), together with measurement nondegeneracy and the subset condition, determines a bijection \(\varphi_{\mathrm{coord}}:\mathscr L(P_X)\to\mathcal Q^K\) uniquely modulo \(\mathfrak G\). Transporting the recovered weights and conditional columns through this bijection identifies \(\Gamma,\pi,p\); faithfulness then identifies \([\Lambda]_{\mathrm{MEC}}\). Thus the passage from \(q^K\) anonymous mixture labels to \(K\) \(q\)-state coordinates and a latent MEC is an additional identification step not supplied by generic three-view Kruskal uniqueness.
body.justification: Anonymous latent-class labels are insufficient for a causal measurement graph; the equality-pattern theorem supplies the missing coordinate product and MEC.
body.gap: Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009) stop at label swapping for one \(q^K\)-class variable, while Kivva et al. (2021) obtain coordinate structure from a supplied mixture oracle; neither proves this observable coordinate-alignment result for certified categorical BLCMs.
body.consumer: It lets an identifiability checker report named latent coordinates, their observed-child sets, and a latent MEC rather than an uninterpreted \(q^K\)-component mixture.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(\mathcal L=\mathscr L(P_X)\).  Membership of \((G,P)\) in
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\), by
Definition~\textnormal{def:certified-class}, entails in particular the
measurement-graph restriction, the Markov factorization, positive latent
support, measurement nondegeneracy, third-view coverage, the subset
condition, and faithfulness.  It also entails
\(\Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}\ne0\), so
Theorem~\textnormal{thm:certificate-frontier} gives
\(\operatorname{rank}(M_1)=\operatorname{rank}(M_2)=q^K\).  The premise of
the present theorem supplies the exact component output: a set
\(\mathcal L\) of \(q^K\) labels and the conditional distribution of each
\(X_j\) in each component, all under one common but unknown permutation of
\(\mathcal Q^K\).

For \(j\in\{1,\ldots,J\}\), define the true latent parent-index set
\[
 A_j=\{k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}:\Gamma_{jk}=1\}.
\]
Fix any bijection \(\psi:\mathcal L\to\mathcal Q^K\) matching the recovered
components to the true latent configurations; such a bijection exists by
the assumed exact component recovery.  Positive latent support guarantees
that every configuration has positive mixing weight, so all conditional
columns used below are defined.  The Markov factorization and the
measurement-graph restriction imply, for every \(h\in\mathcal Q^K\),
\[
 P(X_j=\,\cdot\mid H=h)
 =P(X_j=\,\cdot\mid H_{A_j}=h_{A_j}).
\]
Consequently, if \(h_{A_j}=h'_{A_j}\), the two conditional columns for
\(X_j\) agree.  Conversely, measurement nondegeneracy says that two
distinct configurations of \(H_{A_j}\) induce distinct conditional
distributions.  Thus the observable relation \(E_j\), pulled through
\(\psi\), is exactly
\[
 E_{A_j},\qquad
 h\mathrel{E_A}h' \Longleftrightarrow\ h_A=h'_A
 \quad(A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,K\}).                                      \tag{1}
\]

Order equivalence relations by inclusion as subsets of
\(\mathcal Q^K\times\mathcal Q^K\), and let \(\wedge\) and \(\vee\)
denote their meet and join.  Directly from (1), for all
\(A,B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,K\}\),
\[
 E_A\wedge E_B=E_{A\cup B},
 \qquad
 E_A\vee E_B=E_{A\cap B}.                                               \tag{2}
\]
The first equality is intersection of the two relations.  For the second,
both \(E_A\) and \(E_B\) are contained in \(E_{A\cap B}\), proving one
inclusion.  If \(h\mathrel{E_{A\cap B}}h'\), choose
\(z\in\mathcal Q^K\) by setting \(z_A=h_A\), \(z_B=h'_B\), and assigning
arbitrary states off \(A\cup B\).  The assignments agree on
\(A\cap B\), so they are consistent, and
\(h\mathrel{E_A}z\mathrel{E_B}h'\).  Hence the equivalence relation
generated by \(E_A\cup E_B\) contains \((h,h')\), proving the reverse
inclusion.

Let
\[
 C_k=\{j:k\in A_j\}=\operatorname{ch}_X(H_k).
\]
Third-view coverage makes every \(C_k\) nonempty.  If \(\ell\ne k\), the
subset condition gives \(C_k\not\subseteq C_\ell\); hence some
\(j\in C_k\setminus C_\ell\) contains \(k\) but not \(\ell\) in its
parent set.  It follows that
\[
 \bigcap_{j\in C_k}A_j=\{k\},
 \qquad
 E_{\{k\}}=\bigvee_{j\in C_k}E_j,                                      \tag{3}
\]
where the second equality follows from (2).  Thus every one-coordinate
relation occurs in the finite lattice generated observably by the
\(E_j\)'s.

Moreover, \(E_A\) has exactly \(q^{|A|}\) equivalence classes: its classes
are indexed by the possible values in \(\mathcal Q^A\).  Induction using
(2) shows that every relation in the lattice generated by the \(E_j\)'s is
some \(E_A\).  Since \(q\ge3\), such a relation has exactly \(q\) classes
if and only if \(|A|=1\).  In conjunction with (3), this gives the entirely
observable characterization
\[
 \{E_{\{1\}},\ldots,E_{\{K\}}\}
 =\{F:F\text{ belongs to the generated lattice and has exactly }q
       \text{ classes}\}.                                               \tag{4}
\]

Enumerate the relations in (4) as \(F_1,\ldots,F_K\), and, for each
\(k\), choose a bijection
\(\lambda_k:\mathcal L/F_k\to\mathcal Q\).  Define
\[
 \varphi_{\mathrm{coord}}(\ell)
 =\bigl(\lambda_1([\ell]_{F_1}),\ldots,
          \lambda_K([\ell]_{F_K})\bigr).                                \tag{5}
\]
The meet of the relations in (4) is
\(E_{\{1,\ldots,K\}}\), which is equality on \(\mathcal L\).  Therefore
(5) is injective.  Its domain and codomain each have \(q^K\) elements, so
it is bijective.  The only choices in (5) are the ordering of the \(K\)
relations and the naming of the \(q\) classes of each relation.  These are
exactly a coordinate permutation and an independent state permutation in
each coordinate, namely the action of
\(\mathfrak G=\mathfrak S_K\ltimes(\mathfrak S_q)^K\).  Hence the
coordinate alignment is unique modulo \(\mathfrak G\).

It remains to recover the advertised structure after this alignment.  For
every \(j,k\), equation (1) gives
\[
 k\in A_j\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad E_j\subseteq E_{\{k\}}.           \tag{6}
\]
Indeed, the forward implication follows because agreement on \(A_j\)
implies agreement on coordinate \(k\).  If \(k\notin A_j\), choose two
configurations agreeing on \(A_j\) and differing at \(k\); then the pair
belongs to \(E_j\) but not to \(E_{\{k\}}\), proving the converse.
Formula (6) is an observable recovery map for every row of \(\Gamma\).
Transporting each recovered conditional column through (5) gives
\(p_j(\cdot\mid h)=P(X_j=\,\cdot\mid H=h)\) for all \(j,h\).  The Markov
factorization also gives conditional independence of the observed
coordinates given \(H\), so these columns determine the aligned matrix
\[
 M_1(x,h)=\prod_{j\in S_1}p_j(x_j\mid h).
\]
Let \(v_1\) be the observable probability vector of \(X_{S_1}\), in the
same row order as \(M_1\).  Marginalizing the latent variable gives
\(v_1=M_1\pi\).  Since \(M_1\) has column rank \(q^K\), its Gram matrix is
invertible and hence
\[
 \pi=(M_1^{\mathsf T}M_1)^{-1}M_1^{\mathsf T}v_1.                        \tag{7}
\]
Thus the weights are recovered from \(P_X\), rather than assumed as part of
the decomposition output.  The true weights satisfy (7), and positive
latent support makes every entry strictly positive.  The recovered
\(\Gamma,\pi,p\) are unique subject to the same \(\mathfrak G\)-action.

Finally, the recovered strictly positive table \(\pi\) determines every
latent conditional-independence statement by finite marginalization.  In
particular, every conditioning event in a latent configuration has positive
probability, so the requisite conditional probabilities involve no division
by zero.  For latent vertices and latent conditioning sets, d-separation in
\(G\) is the same as d-separation in \(\Lambda\): by the measurement-graph
restriction, any observed vertex internal to a path between latent vertices
is a sink and hence a collider, and it has no descendants; a path with such
an internal vertex is therefore blocked when conditioning only on latent
vertices.  The remaining paths are precisely the paths in \(\Lambda\),
with unchanged collider status.  Faithfulness of \(P(H,X)\) to \(G\) now
implies that the conditional-independence model computed from \(\pi\) is
exactly the d-separation model of \(\Lambda\).

For completeness, this last recovery is finite and explicit: enumerate all
DAGs on the \(K\) aligned latent vertices and retain those whose
d-separation relations equal the recovered latent conditional-independence
relations.  The true \(\Lambda\) is retained by faithfulness, and
Lemma~\textnormal{lem:dag-markov-equivalence-characterization} says that
all retained DAGs, and only they, have the same skeleton and unshielded
colliders as \(\Lambda\).  They therefore form exactly
\([\Lambda]_{\mathrm{MEC}}\).  Equations (4)--(7), transport of the
conditional columns, and this finite DAG enumeration recover
\([\Gamma,\pi,p,[\Lambda]_{\mathrm{MEC}}]_{\sim}\), proving the claim.
